newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close 1.22 pct lower on pact delay.
newsitem.headline: French shares close 1.22 pct lower on pact delay.

text.p: French shares closed 1.22 percent loweron Monday, but above its lows, after a sudden panic over the future of the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) after France demanded a delay in ratifying the stability pact.
This pact, inspired by Germany, aims to police budgetary discipline among countries which join the single currency.
The CAC-40 index closed down 33.05, or 1.22 percent, at 2,686.2. June futures ended at 2,668.5 against 2,700 at Friday's close.
Volume in CAC-40 shares was 6.8 billion francs and total volume was 8.43 billion francs.
The market opened with an 0.7 percent gain and twice tried to break through the 2,750 level in the morning on continued bullishness after Wall Street's record on Friday on jobs data.
But dealers said the early gains were influenced by the futures market which in turn was powered by short-covering.
Within two hours, EMU jitters set in and shares slipped awaiting news from the Luxembourg finance ministers' meeting.

The blue-chip index fell by 2.2 percent to a day's low of 2,657.07 after France asked for a delay of the European decision on a stability pact because the new Socialist government wanted to consult the National Assembly.

The statement by Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn on his first international appearance caused sharp market and political reactions with Germany insisting the stability pact was needed and non-negotiable while Britain backed him in saying job creation and budget stability were compatible.

European Union President Jacques Santer will come to Paris on Thursday with a compromise for Prime Minister Lionel Jospin. Dealers said the market was likely to remain volatile until after Jospin's general policy statement expected on June 17.
According to Paribas, the market is taking account of the European risk and could fall another 150 points.

Virginie Sue, an economist at Meeschaert Rousselle, said she expected to market to wipe out between now and June 19 the "strange" five percent rally since the parliamentary election which swept the Socialists to power.
